findings.note: Covers lists no expert or computer picks. It shows 61% of user consensus picks on the Over, the Over at 6-0-2 in Washington's last 8 home games, and Washington hitting the Under in only 7 of its last 25. But it quotes the market around o6.0 -120 / u6.5 -120, so 6.5 sits at or above the main line.

Covers' NHL picks hub lists this game's total as U5.5 (-105), which suggests at least one book has the total a full goal below the 6.5 offered here. It also notes the Under is 4-0-1 in Florida's last 5 games as a road favorite, though Florida looks like a slight underdog here.

NHL.com projects Markstrom vs. Thompson in goal and lists Florida without Barkov and Marchand (knee), both not expected to play. Mikkola practiced Friday and is expected to play after taking a shot off his leg.

The NHL.com preview dated Nov. 7, 2026 says Nashville (7-4-5) has won three straight and is 4-1-1 in its last six. Nashville hosts St. Louis at 1 p.m. ET, so the Blues side is facing a home team in good form.

St. Louis lost 3-1 at the Rangers and 5-4 in overtime at New Jersey on this road trip. Logan Mailloux (hand) is back with the team but still on injured reserve. The page lists Nashville at -109 with a 6-goal total.

ESPN has the Blues at 7-7-2, including 3-5-1 on the road, and the Predators at 7-4-5, including 5-3-2 at home. Both moneylines are -110, and Nashville is coming off a 3-2 overtime win over Colorado on a Steven Stamkos goal.

Lightning preview (Nov 6) says Tampa Bay starts a weekend back-to-back in Minnesota and won the Oct. 8 meeting 3-2, a 5-goal game under 6.5, with Hildeby making 34 saves; it does not name tonight's starter.

Covers lists no expert or computer picks; trends point both ways: Over 4-0 in Tampa's last 4 road games, but Under 4-0 in Wild's last 4 vs. Atlantic and 5-1-2 vs. East; consensus splits about evenly on 6.5.
Odds table shows FanDuel at Over 6.0 -122 and theScore Bet at Under 6.5 -120, so other books split between 6 and 6.5 and lean toward the Under at 6.5.

Detroit (7-7-3) lists Dylan Larkin on IR-NR until about Nov 14 and has others on IR, while Colorado (9-6-2, 6-1-2 at home) is missing only Josh Manson and L'Heureux; Colorado scores 4.00 goals per game to Detroit's 2.76, and the Avalanche are about -225.

Detroit goalie John Gibson (lower body) is still being evaluated and missed Thursday's 2-1 loss to Vegas, so the starter is uncertain; Gibson's season save percentage is .860 and backup Tarasov's is .929.
Colorado has lost two straight (7-2 at Columbus, 3-2 in OT to Nashville), but probable starter Blackwood has not allowed more than three goals in any of his last nine games.
